name: Jezebel
bio: Jezebel was the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians, whom Ahab, king of Israel, married — a union Scripture treats as the decisive turn of his reign toward unprecedented evil. Through this marriage Ahab began to serve and worship Baal himself, building a temple and altar for Baal in Samaria and making an Asherah pole, provoking the LORD to anger more than any king of Israel before him (1 Kings 16:31-33). After Elijah's prophets-of-Baal slaughter at Mount Carmel, Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah had done, and she sent him a messenger with a death threat: "So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I make not thy life as the life of one of them by to morrow about this time." The threat worked — Elijah fled for his life all the way to Beersheba and then into the wilderness, eventually reaching Horeb (1 Kings 19:1-8). When Naboth the Jezreelite refused to give up his vineyard to Ahab, Jezebel took charge: she wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal, instructing the elders and nobles of Naboth's city to proclaim a fast, seat him publicly, and have false witnesses accuse him of cursing God and the king so the city would stone him. They did exactly as she ordered, and once Naboth was dead, she told Ahab to go take the vineyard (1 Kings 21:5-15). For this, the LORD pronounced through Elijah that dogs would eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel, and Scripture names her directly as the one who stirred Ahab up to his unmatched wickedness (1 Kings 21:23, 25). Jezebel's further clashes with Elijah, and her lasting infamy, are told in detail in the chapters ahead.
